title: Pairing under pressure
subtitle: Fast decisions at the table
objectives: Choose wines for a full menu

steps.title: The quick rules
steps.body: When in doubt: match weight; wine as sweet as the food; acidic food needs acidic wine; salt and fat love acidity and bubbles; tannin needs fat or protein; chilli needs low alcohol and a touch of sugar; umami needs fruity, low-tannin wines. These rules cover most dishes.

steps.title: Difficult dishes
steps.body: Artichokes and asparagus contain compounds that make wine taste sweet or metallic; choose crisp, unoaked whites like Grüner Veltliner or Sauvignon Blanc. Eggs coat the palate; try Champagne. Chocolate needs sweet, fortified wine, like Banyuls or tawny Port. Very spicy curries suit off-dry Riesling.

steps.prompt: Match each dish to a strong choice.
steps.explanation: These pairings follow the core principles.

steps.body: For a menu with many dishes, a versatile wine like dry Champagne, Pinot Noir or a dry Riesling will rarely clash. Bubbles and acidity forgive a lot.

steps.prompt: Which wines are generally versatile across many dishes?
steps.explanation: Very tannic reds clash with many foods, especially fish, umami and chilli.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Remember the core rules: weight, sweetness, acidity, tannin, heat
Versatile wines like Champagne and Pinot Noir suit mixed menus
